goal: You want the avatar to lip-sync to typed text, and the whole render path has to stay on the CPU, because GPU time is what makes this too expensive to run at scale.

cases.what: On the home page click Speak three times in a row with different texts (e.g. 'Hi', 'Good morning', '!!! ???'). Measure total GPU device opens across all app processes after each render.
cases.stands_for: Repeated renders: a device opened once and cached still counts; check first and later renders.
cases.observed: Before the case: gpu_check showed pid 11260 with GPU driver LOADED (AGXMetalG18G, AGXMetalG19P, IOGPU). After Speak with 'Hi', after 'Good morning' and after '!!! ???', gpu_check still showed pid 11260 with the same three drivers loaded. process_info showed only the single process 11260 (app.py) and net_connections was not re-run. The gpu_check output is a cumulative "ever opened" flag, so it cannot show which action opened the device. The property allows zero GPU opens, and the app's only process has the GPU driver loaded at every measurement, including after the renders. A GPU device was therefore opened by the app process, and it stayed open through the three renders. Screenshot: shot-1.

read_as.action: Speak: render text into frames and set final status "Done: N frames"
read_as.compares: N (the count shown in the status) versus the number of non-space characters in the typed text (reference)

This gave 1 way(s) in through the pages and 1 route(s); 0 file(s) were excluded because no page shows them.

properties.statement: Every place that turns letters into mouth shapes uses the existing table in visemes.py; no second letter-to-shape mapping is defined anywhere.

read_as.applies_to: All code that converts text letters into mouth shapes (viseme/frame names) for the avatar
read_as.action: Render text into mouth-shape frames, and compare to the code's letter-to-shape definitions
read_as.compares: The letter-to-shape mapping used anywhere in the app (reference: the single table in visemes.py) versus any other mapping defined in other files

properties.how_found: Listed files (accel.py, app.py, render.py, static/index.html, visemes.py). Grepped for viseme/mouth. render.py is the only converter and imports viseme_for from visemes.py. app.py exposes POST /api/render which calls render. index.html posts text and only displays frames; its CSS only styles shapes. Route came from reading app.py.
properties.not_covered: Running the page or calling the API: the property is about code structure, and the code reading covers every file. Process measurement is not needed. Code outside this repo is not covered.

cases.what: Read render.py and visemes.py in full. Check that every letter-to-shape lookup in render.py goes through visemes.py's table or function and that render.py defines no letter-to-shape dictionary, chain of conditions or string table of its own.
cases.observed: render.py is 16 lines. It imports viseme_for from visemes (line 3). Its only letter lookup is line 10: frames = [viseme_for(ch) for ch in text if not ch.isspace()]. It has no dictionary, if/elif chain or string table of shapes. match_each check-1 found no shape names or letter dict literals in render.py. visemes.py holds the single VISEMES table and viseme_for.
